parole.testo: Possibly related to lonkata (“to limp”), which is a Finnic word in origin. Origin from Proto-West Germanic *hlanku (“bend, curve, hip, flank”) is also possible, but is rejected by LÄGLOS.

parole.significato: Monday (day of the week; the first day of the week in Finland and in the ISO 8601 standard)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Old Swedish mānadagher, or from Middle Low German māndach; ultimately from Proto-West Germanic *mānini dag.

parole.significato: Friday (day of the week; the fifth day of the week in Finland and in the ISO 8601 standard)
parole.testo: Borrowed from North Germanic, probably Old Swedish frē(i)adagher, frīadagher; ultimately from Proto-West Germanic *Frījā dag. Details Since Finnish historically lacks f and initial consonant clusters (such as fr), the word was adapted to fit the language's phonological rules, with f- becoming p- and
